editorial:
Imagine you are a photographer who is bored with normal pictures and only wants to capture the darkest parts of the city. That is exactly where you start with this story. You follow a guy who gets too curious about a series of murders happening on the subway late at night. The vibe is gritty, dirty, and honestly pretty creepy. You feel the tension as he tracks a killer who uses a giant meat hook to take out commuters. It starts as a mystery but quickly turns into a wild ride that pushes the limits of how much blood you can stomach.

What really works here is how the movie keeps you guessing about who the killer actually is. The acting is solid, and the pacing moves fast enough that you will not get bored. The big twist at the end is totally unexpected and changes everything you thought you knew. If you love gore and weird stories, you should definitely check this out. You can rent it on Apple TV for a quick movie night, or if you are a collector, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is the way to go to see all those gross details clearly.
endingExplained: You find out the killer is not actually a human man, but a monster that feeds the subway system. The train is actually a living creature that needs blood to keep running. The killer is just its servant. In the end, the main character kills the monster, but he is forced to take its place. He becomes the new killer to keep the city's trains moving, meaning the cycle just starts all over again.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves gore and twist endings.
